abilitygroupdescription.p: The primary abilities are six core abilities that represent the characters raw, innate, unlearned capabilities. Fortune also makes this list though it is singular enough not to be considered a primary ability and arguably not an ability at all. sec:primary_abilities

Checks Ability
Ability Check
Primary Ability Check
Primary Ability Checks are ability checks, made using one of the characters primary abilities, Strength, Endurance, Agility, etc. Primary Ability checks are usually used when no more specific check can be applied, a character might check using their Agility when trying to catch a falling object as there is no catch ability. A check whether a character can make it to shore from a sinking ship should be made using the Swim ability and not the endurance primary ability, since the Swim ability is more specific in this case.

playexample.p: Dourli tries to shift a large wine barrel that is sitting on a trap door in a cellar. The GM declares that in order to do so Dourli must make a Strength Check with a difficulty of 12. The player rolls a 9 for their Outcome. Dourli has Strength 2, and so gets a total of 11. Dourli fails to move the wine barrel. If he had a Strength 3 he would have succeeded.

ability.slug: To crush your enemies, see them driven before you, and to hear the lamentations of their women

abilitydescription.p: Strength represents the characters brute physical power. Strength saves are made when the character wishes to perform a Feat of Strength, such as bending bars, opening doors and to lift heavy objects. Strength modifies the characters Health and melee damage for some weapons.

ability.slug: In the fell clutch of circumstance I have not winced nor cried aloud. Under the bludgeonings of chance My head is bloody, but unbowed.

abilitydescription.p:
Endurance
Abilities Endurance
Endurance is the characters ability to handle physical stress. If a character has a high endurance it indicates that they are healthy and tough. Endurance is used to save against poisons, resist exhaustion, diseases, the cold, and modifies the characters Stamina.

Agility
Abilities Agility
Acrobatics (use Agility)
Agility represents the characters ability to move easily; their nimbleness, athleticism and dexterity.
The Sure-Feet specialization is used when the character makes an agility save to avoid being knocked prone.

ability.slug: Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast.

abilitydescription.p:
Speed
Abilities Speed
Movement see Speed
Jumping (use Speed)
Speed determines how physically fast the character is. Speed checks are made for characters attempting to sprint, jump, or fleeing.

Perception
Abilities Perception
Spot Hidden use Perception
Initiative see Perception
Notice (use Perception)
Listen (use Perception)
The character's awareness, acumen and insight. Perception represents your attentiveness to detail and your unflagging vigilance. In game this value is used socially, for reading people and detecting underhanded motives. Perception modifies checks used both for surveying the surrounds for potential avenues of attack, and reduces the likelihood of being surprised, for searching.
Perception can be used in social situations to see if a person is being deceptive.

ability.slug: Everything you've ever wanted is on the other side of fear.

action.name: Break Save
action.fail: Another local ally makes a break check.

action.name: Magic Save
action.effect:
Magic Resilience
Characters make a magic check to overcome the effects of magic cast against them.

abilitydescription.p:
Will
Abilities Will
Will represents the characters strength of character. Their grit and determination. Will is often used when making Mettle Checks.

Characters may, from time to time, be forced to make a Break Save. Break saves occur when characters have to face their fears as determined by the GM. In addition some abilities target the opponents Mettle, Banish, and Howl of the Hunt forcing a Break Save.

A break save is a check made against the Mettle Pool. When a character fails a Mettle Check another nearby character, chosen at random or by the GM, must also make a break check. Break checks can continue to cascade until someone succeeds or everyone in the group has failed.

The GM should feel free to modify the target SV as he pleases, to reflect being attacked at night, being vastly outnumbered, the horrible visage of the characters opponents, the party being in good spirits etc. As characters fail break checks the party starts to lose points from their mettle pools and their fighting options diminish.

Some suggested times to make break checks are:
Whenever the first party member becomes bloodied,
When the party enters combat against a fear causing opponent, and
Whenever the party is Surprised or Ambushed.
Ultimately, however, it is up to the GMs discretion to decide when the players should make a break checks and the GM should feel free to force break checks sooner or later in the combat to satisfy the narrative imperative.

The first time the group collectively fails a break check then everyone gains the Checked Condition see pagecondition:checked, the second time everyone fails a break check everyone gains the Broken Condition, see pagecondition:broken. The third time the group fails their break check they gain the Routed Condition, see pagecondition:routed.

playexample.p: Dourli and Rozlyn have been fighting a running battle with the Black Mark and it's starting to take its toll on the two. Rozlyn is hit with an arrow, dropping her Stamina to zero, giving her the bloodied condition. The GM determines that Rozyln should make a break save. She fails, so Dourli now has to make one. He too fails. Now they both gain the broken condition and have lost mettle in the process.

ability.slug: On what slender threads do life and fortune hang!

abilitydescription.p:
Fortune Save
Saves Fortune
Characters make a Fortune Save to see if luck smiles upon them. Whenever the GM finds themselves in a situation where they turn to a player and ask Do you feel lucky? then perhaps the player should be making a Fortune Save.
Fortune cannot be trained. Its rank is always zero and it is available to all PCs.

playexample.p: Dourli is sitting in a corner tied up by the Black Mark, waiting on an uncertain fate. A lone guard, in his cups, watches over him. Dourli wonders whether the guard might need to leave momentarily to relieve himself. The GM determines that since Dourli has been tied up for a long time and the the guard is drinking, chances are high that the guard will leave the room for a short time at some point. So he allows Dourli to make a fortune save, shifted up. Dourli's current luck pool is 1. He rolls and gets a 12. Dourli's luck pool is reduced by one to zero. Dourli is lucky, just, thanks to the shift, and he takes his opportunity when the guard leaves to answer the call of nature, bolting for it, his arms still tied.
